topic.title: Text-Conditioned Diffusion and Concept Control
topic.overview: Text-to-image diffusion models connect linguistic descriptions to visual generation through learned conditioning and denoising dynamics. This topic studies architecture, semantic guidance, text embeddings, scaling, and targeted concept modification. A recurring challenge is controlling one concept while preserving the model’s broader ability to generate coherent images.
topic.whyItMatters: Strong average image quality can coexist with weak handling of rare semantics or unwanted memorization. Understanding where text and image information interact helps design changes that affect the intended content without collapsing generation.
topic.evolution: The collection begins with early zero-shot and diffusion-based text-to-image systems in 2021–2022. Later work improves semantic guidance and rectified-flow Transformers. Recent papers examine rare concepts, layer-specific erasure, and single-stream architectures, where shared text-image parameters make selective modification especially delicate.
openQuestions: How can concept removal be evaluated beyond a small set of prompts?
Which internal representations support precise semantic control without damaging unrelated content?
